query: Which paired permutation/bootstrap test statistics and multiple-testing correction procedures provide reproducible comparisons between interval methods, and what reference implementations and power analyses are required?

response.query: Which paired permutation/bootstrap test statistics and multiple-testing correction procedures provide reproducible comparisons between interval methods, and what reference implementations and power analyses are required?
response.answer: Paired permutation and bootstrap test statistics with multiple-testing corrections like Bonferroni or Benjamini-Hochberg are reproducible. R packages like "coin" and "boot" provide implementations. Power analyses often use simulations to validate these methods.

results.title: Bioconductor 3.9 Released
results.content: There are 105 new software packages, 13 new data experiment packages, 4 new workflows, and many updates and improvements to existing packages; Bioconductor 3.9 is compatible with R 3.6.0, and is supported on Linux, 32- and 64-bit Windows, and Mac OS X. * New Data Experiment Packages * animalcules animalcules is an R package for utilizing up-to-date data analytics, visualization methods, and machine learning models to provide users an easy-to-use interactive microbiome analysis framework. * CellBench This package contains infrastructure for benchmarking analysis methods and access to single cell mixture benchmarking data. * deco This package discovers differential features in hetero- and homogeneous omic data by a two-step method including subsampling LIMMA and NSCA. * Add dirname and dirname<- methods for OnDiskMSnExp to change the path to the raw data files. * Add correspondence analysis (peak grouping) for chromatographic data (for now only with PeakDensity method; issue #336).

results.title: What do you believe is true though you can't prove it?
results.content: I believe that human talents are based on distinct patterns of brain connectivity. Most cognitive scientists believe that consciousness is a phenomenon that emerges from the complex interaction of decidedly nonconscious parts (neurons), but even when we finally understand the nature of that complex interaction, we still won't be able to prove that it produces the phenomenon in question. I mean that I am convinced that there is a consistent way of thinking about nature, that makes no use of the notions of space and time at the fundamental level. I believe, but cannot prove, that memory is inherent in nature. Just making the right proteins at the right times cannot explain such structures without many other forces coming into play, including the organizing activity of cell membranes and microtubules. But whatever the details of the models, I believe that the natural selection of habits will play an essential part in any integrated theory of evolution, including not just biological evolution, but also physical, chemical, cosmic, social, mental and cultural evolution.
